newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economic growth seen failing to create jobs.
newsitem.headline: German economic growth seen failing to create jobs.

text.p: The German economy will gather steam in 1997, but remain too weak to reduce unemployment, the German Economics Insitute (IW) said on Thursday.
The institute said the main engine of growth would remain exports but that growth in the sector would be slower than overall growth in world international trade.
Economic growth, the report said, would not be strong enough to reduce unemployment below the four million mark.
Private consumption, which many economists are counting on to lift the economy, should climb by more than two percent.
Higher incomes, slow increases in the prices of goods and confidence in the economy should make consumers more willing to spend, IW said.
Consumer prices should pose little threat to economic stability, climbing about 1.5 percent in 1997, the report went on.
